bug_semantics: When the root shard embedded the cache server, it mounted the cache handler at /services/cache/ on preHandlerChainMux, which runs before the root shard's authentication and authorization chain. The cache server's own Complete method explicitly nulled its authentication and authorization options, so an unauthenticated network client reaching the root shard could read replicated control-plane data and issue writes; malicious RBAC writes could briefly influence shared authorization informers before the replication controller deleted them.
flaw_origin: Commit e426bc4e86f34af728e479e6b951f1c12b8b0ccd first inserted `if s.Options.Cache.Enabled { s.installCacheServer(ctx) }` into Server.Run but did not define installCacheServer (pkg/server/cache.go absent). The next first-parent commits still lack the method until 44b4682b63e6edbc4f63014adfa27d395ea958c2, which adds pkg/server/cache.go, mounts preparedCacheServer.Handler at /services/cache/ on preHandlerChainMux, and thereby first makes the unauthenticated cache path reachable. Immediate parent 812c0caeed040f672e2315012f3e1f4b07d4f9d7 has the call and no Handle registration. Cache.Enabled defaulted false until later fe14d33b31eabb410c5e1f0e5c3396cc1cdf60f9 made embedded cache mandatory; that is not the first-write.
ai_marker: absent: raw commit object 44b4682b63e6edbc4f63014adfa27d395ea958c2 names Lukasz Szaszkiewicz <lukasz.szaszkiewicz@gmail.com> as both author and committer; message is 'kcp: install the cache-server' plus a two-line body, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: GitHub advisory https://github.com/kcp-dev/kcp/security/advisories/GHSA-3j3q-wp9x-585p is published (withdrawn_at null). CVE.org/cveawg record CVE-2026-39429 has cveMetadata.state PUBLISHED and describes unauthenticated cache-server access on the root shard.
